title: Jira vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Jira vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Jira and Plane are two project management tools that help teams organize and track their work. This comparison is useful for teams considering switching from Jira to Plane, particularly those looking for a self-hosted solution with more control over their data. The core use case for both tools is issue tracking and project management, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more flexibility and autonomy over their data.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Jira is a paid service with a per-user monthly fee, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Plane allows teams to have full ownership and control over their data, while Jira stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Plane requires more technical expertise to set up and maintain, while Jira is easier to get started with.
* Scalability: Jira is designed to scale with large teams and enterprises, while Plane is better suited for smaller teams and self-hosted environments.
* Integration with GitHub: Jira has a more comprehensive integration with GitHub, while Plane's integration is more limited.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Jira | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.75-$14.50/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $387.50-$725.00/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,550.00-$2,900.00/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Jira:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Comprehensive integration with GitHub
* Scalable for large teams and enterprises
* Wide range of plugins and integrations available
* Good customer support
**Plane:**
* Free and self-hosted
* Full control over data ownership and security
* Customizable and flexible
* Open-source and community-driven
* Limited integration with GitHub

## When to Choose Each
Jira is a good choice for large teams and enterprises that need a scalable and comprehensive project management solution. It is also a good fit for teams that are already invested in the Atlassian ecosystem and want to take advantage of its integrations with other tools. On the other hand, Plane is a good choice for smaller teams and self-hosted environments that want more control over their data and security. It is also a good fit for teams that are looking for a free and open-source solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Jira in CSV or JSON format.
2. Use the Plane import tool to import your data into Plane.
3. Configure your Plane instance to match your Jira workflow and settings.
4. Test and verify that all your data and workflows have been successfully migrated.
5. Update any integrations or plugins to work with Plane.

## Our Take
Plane is not yet production-ready for most users, as it lacks some of the features and polish of Jira. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Plane's integration with GitHub is limited, which may be a deal-breaker for teams that rely heavily on GitHub. However, for teams that value self-hosting and data ownership, Plane is a compelling alternative to Jira, and we recommend considering it as an option.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that don't need advanced features like workflow automation
* Self-hosted environments that want full control over their data and security
* Teams that are already using other open-source tools and want to integrate with Plane
* Developers who want a customizable and flexible project management solution
* Teams that are looking for a free and open-source alternative to Jira

## FAQ
### Can I use Plane for free?
Yes, Plane is free and self-hosted, which means you can use it without paying any monthly fees.
### Is Plane as scalable as Jira?
No, Plane is not yet as scalable as Jira, and is better suited for smaller teams and self-hosted environments.
### Can I integrate Plane with GitHub?
Yes, Plane has a limited integration with GitHub, but it is not as comprehensive as Jira's integration.
### Is Plane production-ready?
Not yet, Plane is still in development and lacks some of the features and polish of Jira.
### Can I migrate my data from Jira to Plane?
Yes, you can export your data from Jira in CSV or JSON format and import it into Plane using the Plane import tool.

title: Trello vs WeKan
comparison_markdown:
# Trello vs WeKan

## Overview

Trello is a visual kanban board tool from Atlassian, simple and beginner-friendly. WeKan is an open-source kanban board offering the same card/list/board model without vendor dependency.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Trello paid plans start at $5/user/month; WeKan is completely free
- **Data control**: WeKan runs on your own server; Trello data lives on Atlassian infrastructure
- **Features**: Trello has a larger Power-Ups marketplace; WeKan covers core kanban features
- **Setup**: Trello requires zero setup; WeKan requires a server
- **Customization**: WeKan open-source code can be extended; Trello cannot

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Trello | WeKan |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $5+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Trello

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### WeKan

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [wekan/wekan](https://github.com/wekan/wekan) * ~20k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Trello if:** Trello suits individuals and small teams wanting instant zero-setup kanban with integrations to Slack, Google Drive, and GitHub.

**Choose WeKan if:** WeKan is ideal for teams wanting full data ownership or air-gapped deployments.

## Migration Path

Export Trello boards as JSON, then use WeKan Trello importer in Settings to recreate boards, lists, and cards.

## Our Take

WeKan is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Trello tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your WeKan instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Trello, switching to self-hosted WeKan will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Trello until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Trello paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is WeKan free to use?
Yes. WeKan is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Trello to WeKan?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Trello data, follow the WeKan import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does WeKan get regular updates?
Yes. WeKan has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use WeKan without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if WeKan development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Trello](https://trello.com) and [WeKan](https://wekan.github.io) before making decisions.*
meta_description: WeKan is a free, self-hosted alternative to Trello. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

title: Dropbox vs Nextcloud
comparison_markdown:
# Dropbox vs Nextcloud (2026)

## Overview
Dropbox and Nextcloud are cloud storage solutions that enable individuals and teams to store, share, and collaborate on files. This comparison is beneficial for individuals and organizations seeking to switch from a proprietary cloud storage solution to a self-hosted alternative. The core use case for both tools is file storage and sharing, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Dropbox charges a monthly fee per user, while Nextcloud is free to use with self-hosting.
* Data ownership: Nextcloud allows users to retain full ownership of their data, whereas Dropbox's terms of service grant the company certain rights to user data.
* Setup complexity: Nextcloud requires more technical expertise to set up and maintain, especially for self-hosting, compared to Dropbox's straightforward sign-up process.
* Scalability: Nextcloud can be more scalable than Dropbox, especially for large organizations, since it can be self-hosted on the user's own servers.
* Integration with calendar and contacts: Nextcloud offers more extensive integration with calendar and contacts through its own applications, whereas Dropbox relies on third-party integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Dropbox | Nextcloud |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $9.99-$16.58/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $499.50-$829/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $1,998-$3,316/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Dropbox:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of third-party integrations
* Robust security features
* Good customer support
* Limited control over data ownership
**Nextcloud:**
* Self-hosting option for full data control
* High scalability and customization
* Extensive integration with calendar and contacts
* Free to use with self-hosting
* Requires technical expertise for setup and maintenance

## When to Choose Each
Dropbox is suitable for small to medium-sized teams that prioritize ease of use and do not require full control over their data. It is also a good choice for individuals who need a simple, user-friendly cloud storage solution. On the other hand, Nextcloud is ideal for large organizations or teams that require high scalability, customization, and control over their data. It is also a good choice for individuals or teams that value data ownership and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining a self-hosted solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Dropbox in ZIP format.
2. Set up a Nextcloud instance on your own server or use a pre-configured appliance.
3. Use the Nextcloud importer tool to import your data from the ZIP file.
4. Configure any additional features or integrations as needed.
5. Test your Nextcloud instance to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
Nextcloud is a production-ready solution for most users, offering a high degree of customization and control over data. However, it is essential to be aware of the technical expertise required for setup and maintenance. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Nextcloud's user management features can be complex to configure for large organizations. We recommend switching to Nextcloud for users who value data ownership and are willing to invest time and resources into setup and maintenance, but advise against switching for small teams or individuals who prioritize ease of use.

## Who Should Switch
* Large organizations with over 100 users that require high scalability and customization
* Teams that require full control over their data and are willing to invest time and resources into setup and maintenance
* Individuals who value data ownership and are technically inclined
* Organizations that do not require extensive customer support
* Teams that need extensive integration with calendar and contacts

## FAQ
### Can I use Nextcloud for free?
Yes, Nextcloud is free to use with self-hosting, but you will need to cover the costs of server maintenance and upkeep.
### Is Nextcloud more secure than Dropbox?
Nextcloud offers a high degree of security, but the level of security ultimately depends on the user's setup and configuration.
### Can I migrate my data from Dropbox to Nextcloud?
Yes, you can export your data from Dropbox and import it into Nextcloud using the importer tool.
### Does Nextcloud offer customer support?
Nextcloud offers community support and paid support options for enterprises, but it may not be as extensive as Dropbox's customer support.
### Is Nextcloud suitable for small teams?
Nextcloud can be suitable for small teams, but it may require more technical expertise and resources than Dropbox.
meta_description: Nextcloud, a free self-hosted cloud storage solution, offers data ownership and scalability. See full comparison or Free migration guide.

# Zoom vs Jitsi Meet (2026)

## Overview
Zoom and Jitsi Meet are video conferencing tools that enable teams to collaborate remotely. This comparison is beneficial for teams and individuals looking to switch from a proprietary platform to a self-hosted solution or seeking more control over their data. The core use case for both tools is virtual meetings, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more flexibility and autonomy over their video conferencing experience.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Zoom offers a free plan with limited features, while Jitsi Meet is completely free and open-source.
* Data Ownership: Jitsi Meet allows users to self-host their servers, giving them full control over their data, whereas Zoom stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup Complexity: Jitsi Meet requires more technical expertise to set up, especially for self-hosting, compared to Zoom's straightforward sign-up process.
* Scalability: Zoom is designed to handle large-scale meetings and webinars, while Jitsi Meet can also scale but may require more configuration and resources.
* Feature Difference: Zoom offers more advanced features like virtual whiteboards and polls, whereas Jitsi Meet focuses on providing a simple, secure, and customizable video conferencing experience.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Zoom | Jitsi Meet |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $13.33+/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $666.50/month (50 users \* $13.33) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $2,666/month (200 users \* $13.33) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Zoom:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Advanced features like virtual whiteboards and polls
* Large user base and community support
* Scalable and reliable
* Integrates with many third-party tools
* Limited control over data and security
**Jitsi Meet:**
* Self-hosting option for full data control
* Free and open-source
* Customizable and secure
* Simple and intuitive interface
* Limited advanced features compared to Zoom
* Requires technical expertise for self-hosting

## When to Choose Each
Zoom is suitable for large teams and enterprises that require advanced features, scalability, and ease of use. It's ideal for teams that don't mind using a proprietary platform and are willing to pay for the convenience and reliability it offers. On the other hand, Jitsi Meet is perfect for small to medium-sized teams, individuals, or organizations that value data sovereignty, security, and customization. It's also a great option for teams with technical expertise who want to self-host their video conferencing solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Zoom meeting recordings and data in MP4 and CSV formats.
2. Set up a Jitsi Meet server using a cloud provider or self-hosting on your own infrastructure.
3. Use the Jitsi Meet import tool to import your user data and meeting schedules.
4. Configure your Jitsi Meet instance to suit your team's needs, including customizing the interface and setting up security measures.
5. Test your Jitsi Meet setup to ensure a smooth transition from Zoom.

## Our Take
Jitsi Meet is not yet production-ready for most users due to its limited user interface and lack of advanced features. However, it's a great option for teams that value security and data control. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Jitsi Meet requires a strong understanding of networking and server configuration to set up and maintain. We recommend switching to Jitsi Meet if you're a small team or individual who values data sovereignty and security, but if you're a large enterprise that relies on advanced features, Zoom might still be the better choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who don't need advanced features like virtual whiteboards
* Individuals who value data sovereignty and security
* Organizations with technical expertise who want to self-host their video conferencing solution
* Teams who require customization and flexibility in their video conferencing experience
* Users who don't need integration with third-party tools like calendars or CRM systems

## FAQ
### Can I use Jitsi Meet for free?
Yes, Jitsi Meet is completely free and open-source, with no costs or licensing fees.
### Is Jitsi Meet secure?
Yes, Jitsi Meet is designed with security in mind, offering end-to-end encryption and secure data storage.
### Can I self-host Jitsi Meet?
Yes, Jitsi Meet offers a self-hosting option, allowing you to run your own server and have full control over your data.
### Does Jitsi Meet integrate with calendar apps?
Not yet, but Jitsi Meet has an open API and is working on integrating with popular calendar apps.
### Can I use Jitsi Meet for large-scale webinars?
Not recommended, as Jitsi Meet is designed for smaller meetings and may not handle large-scale webinars as well as Zoom.
